correctness.rationale: The complete proof derives the characteristic polynomial, exact S1/S2 moment identities and S4 endpoint asymptotic. Rouché inversion controls the winding-one eigenpair at complex scale 1/(N log N). A strict monotone modulus/argument curve proves this pair dominates every other nonstationary eigenvalue, not merely that it exists. Fourth-order expansion of the logarithmic modulus yields the explicit negative π^8/90 correction with O(1/(N H_N^6)) remainder. The reproducibility script passed rational identities and finite complex-root checks; those checks do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary paper supplies the same exact characteristic polynomial and a second-order heuristic leading gap. Its approximation assumes small individual jump probabilities, whereas at the joint-size positivity boundary the maximum equals one for odd dimensions. It neither proves subdominant modulus ordering in that regime nor gives the negative fourth-moment term −π^8/[90(N+1)H_N^5]. Targeted published-result searches found no equivalent stronger claim; background cyclic-chain spectral arguments do not by themselves imply this model-specific two-term constant. Priority cannot be guaranteed.

value.rationale: The positivity boundary is the natural joint-size operating regime for the Dicke-preparation protocol, distinct from the source’s fixed-normalization finite admissible window. Identifying the exact spectral pair and fourth-moment correction determines the true sharp relaxation exponent where small-jump expansions cease to apply. The squared-logarithmic separation between mean circulation and relaxation quantifies a previously unresolved operational bottleneck and yields a nontrivial worst-start mixing-time lower bound.
